# Concept bubbles

> Concept bubbles is the application of unsymbolized thinking to learning. A concept bubble is one idea held in unsymbolized thinking, with no words and no picture. Learners hold each idea or flashcard as a concept bubble and link it to the one before.

Unsymbolized thinking is the psychologist Russell Hurlburt’s name for a clear, specific thought that comes without words or pictures. No one has yet tested it as a study technique; thoughtfeel works with students and teachers to do that. Just as people can imagine in pictures or in sounds, people with unsymbolized thinking can imagine in concepts. Hurlburt named and studies unsymbolized thinking. The concept bubbles technique was developed by Ted Shachtman, and Hurlburt isn’t involved in it.

Not everyone has unsymbolized thinking. Like vision and hearing, it differs from person to person, and it most likely varies the way the mind’s eye does. In the best-known study, 22 of 30 college students had at least one moment of it in about ten random samples each; some had it in none of their moments and one in 80% of them. There is no figure yet for how many people in general have it. (Source: Russell Hurlburt’s study of inner experience, Heavey & Hurlburt, 2008, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.concog.2007.12.006. 22 of 30 people had unsymbolized thinking at least once.)

thoughtfeel.net is a practical guide to the technique, by Ted Shachtman.

## The earlier name

From September to November 2026 the technique, and the kind of thinking it uses, were both called thoughtfeel. Since November 2026 the technique is called concept bubbles, and the kind of thinking goes by its research name, unsymbolized thinking. The videos and posts from before then still say thoughtfeel. thoughtfeel is still the name of the site (thoughtfeel.net) and of the YouTube channel (youtube.com/@ThoughtFeelGuide).

What a concept bubble is not:

- Not a diagram or a mind map. Nothing is drawn. A concept bubble is held in your mind. The lessons show bubbles on screen only to point at which concept is meant.
- Not your mind’s eye or inner voice. Pictures and words can come along with a thought, but a concept bubble works without them.
- Not an emotion. The economy and justice feel different from each other, but neither one feels happy or sad.
- Not the feeling of knowing. Everyone knows what they’re thinking. A concept bubble gives the thought itself detail you can notice, the way a picture has detail.
- Not the same thing as unsymbolized thinking. Unsymbolized thinking is the kind of thought. Concept bubbles is the technique that uses it on purpose, the way the memory palace uses the mind’s eye.

## The definition

- [What are concept bubbles?](https://thoughtfeel.net/concept-bubbles/): the definition, with examples, and what a concept bubble is not

## Can you do it?

- [The one-question quiz](https://thoughtfeel.net/quiz/): the four ways to think about your best friend (a picture, their voice, just knowing, a concept bubble); if you can get a sense of the fourth, you can use concept bubbles
